answer: The spiral detector writes to forge, and delta reveals every merge. A farm scripting its whole swarm fires them together, thus the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 111 aliases out costs the operator real scheduling effort per key. Submissions that land within 81 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. That is 7 dollars per alias. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
